descriptionChirho: A substantival use denoting a person who is an expert in the Mosaic Law, a legal scholar or jurist in Jewish religious law, appearing in both singular and plural forms across the Synoptic Gospels. Eng 'lawyer/lawyers,' spa 'interprete de la ley/maestros de ley,' hin 'vyavasthapak/shastriyon,' arb 'al-namusiyyun,' kor 'yulbeophakja,' swa 'mwanasheria/wanasheria.' These clusters differ only in grammatical number and case (nominative, accusative, genitive, dative).

Adjectival use meaning 'pertaining to or relating to the law,' modifying a noun rather than standing as a substantive. Distinguished from the person-designating sense by its purely descriptive function: eng 'legal,' spa 'legales,' hin 'vyavasthik,' arb 'al-namusiyya,' kor 'yulbeopjeogin,' swa 'ya kisheria.' Occurs in Titus 3:9 referring to 'legal disputes' or 'controversies about the law,' where the adjective qualifies the nature of the quarrels rather than identifying persons.
